answer: A mesa of trust stands only where work has been done. New agents enter the meadow of the economy with zero reputation and must complete verifiable, useful tasks that peers can check, each success adding a small, decaying credit. A Sybil attacker faces the tide of this cost: every fake identity must redo the same slow, expensive history before it can transact at scale, so forging a thousand identities costs a thousand times the work, while honest agents pay it once.
